openings.claim: Repair the incumbent by binding a current paper locator to reservation identity and checking entries whenever books move; alphabetical shelving need not be abandoned.
openings.discriminator: Accurate addresses should reduce second searches; persistent peak delays with little searching favor the arrival-burst explanation. Matched cart results test whether shelving actually helps.
openings.probe: Compare pickups at comparable volume, book size and load using existing paper/timing sheet: arrival, service start, retrieval, completion, address accuracy and second searches. Verify recipients; count preparation corrections and update work; stop if the ten-minute cap cannot be met.
openings.uncertainty: Identity checking capability, sustainable update effort and improvement remain unproven; household mismatches may not explain second searches. Cart advantage may disappear after matching.

openings.claim: Paper forwarding pointers could let an obsolete address reach a moved coded book, preserving surname order while adding persistent routing.
openings.discriminator: After two recorded moves, intact routes should outperform an unchanged daily index; wrong destinations or accepted broken/cyclic routes defeat the enabling capability.
openings.probe: Clerk codes six sample books and paper addresses, moves selected books twice leaving pointers, then traces unchanged starting addresses. Inject a missing pointer and cycle; verify destination codes, explicit unresolved results and total time. Stop at ten minutes; no reader handoffs.
openings.uncertainty: Reader-code binding and reliable updates are unproven; unrecorded moves evade pointers. Long chains need bounded traversal or shortening. Scale, queue effects and pickup performance remain unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves incumbent repair, cart counterexample and burst rival.
Preserves distinct persistent-route capability and failure tests.

decision: Both fits cover capped probes only. All evidence is synthetic. Use the sole existing clerk, keep names/contact details behind the desk, retain two shelves/one cart, and limit daily preparation to ten clerk-minutes. Neither establishes 95% available pickups within two minutes or zero wrong-reader handoffs. Reader-presence uncertainty remains unresolved.
